text:
Nikita Kucherov is playing out the strangest stretch of a Hall of Fame career. On Oct. 30 he told the Lightning he won't re-sign and asked for a trade, according to the Associated Press, and Tampa's general manager Julien BriseBois has said publicly he has no intention of moving him. Meanwhile the reigning Hart Trophy winner keeps doing his job: 22 points in 17 games, 14 of them in the last ten, including an overtime winner in Minnesota.

The numbers say there is more to come, not less. He is shooting 9.8% against a typical range of 13 to 17%, and his scoring rate of 3.65 points per 60 sits below the band our talent range expects from him. Evolving-Hockey had him second among all forwards in wins above replacement last season, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking still has him among the best setup men in the league.

What to watch: whether the goals catch up before the standoff resolves. Our projection still lands him around 123 points. Whoever ends up with him is getting a player who has not slowed down.
headline: Kucherov keeps producing while asking out
